test_title: PYST 34: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 19 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In March 2025, what important decision did the Supreme Court of India make regarding disability rights?

options.text: It allowed only private companies to hire persons with disabilities.
It said disability rights are a part of fundamental rights.
It removed reservations for persons with disabilities.
It banned all exams for persons with disabilities.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It said disability rights are a part of fundamental rights.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Supreme Court of India, in March 2025, declared that **disability rights are an integral part of fundamental rights** under the Indian Constitution.
 
• This landmark decision emphasized the enforcement of the **Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016**, ensuring equality, dignity, and inclusion for persons with disabilities.
 
• The judgment underscored Article 21 of the Constitution, which guarantees the **right to life with dignity**, and linked it to the rights of individuals with disabilities.
 
• It mandated that public and private entities must ensure **reasonable accommodations** for persons with disabilities to eliminate discrimination.
 
• The ruling reinforced the idea that **accessibility, equal opportunities, and non-discrimination** are essential for fostering an inclusive society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (RPwD Act):**

 
 
• It replaced the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights, and Full Participation) Act, 1995.
 
• The Act recognizes 21 types of disabilities, including mental illness, autism, and dwarfism.
 
• It ensures rights such as education, employment, and social security for persons with disabilities.
 
• It mandates a reservation of **4% in government jobs** and **5% in educational institutions** for persons with benchmark disabilities.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights under the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• Fundamental rights are guaranteed under Articles 12–35 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 21 guarantees the **right to life and personal liberty**, which includes the right to live with dignity.
 
• Equality before law (Article 14) and prohibition of discrimination (Article 15) are key provisions supporting disability rights.
 
 
 
• **Reasonable Accommodation:**
 
 
• It refers to necessary and appropriate modifications to ensure persons with disabilities can enjoy their rights equally.
 
• Examples include ramps in buildings, assistive technologies, or extended time during examinations.
 
 
 
• **Global Framework on Disability Rights:**
 
 
• The United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD) was adopted in 2006.
 
• India ratified the UNCRPD in 2007, committing to its principles of equality, non-discrimination, and accessibility.
